blocks.html: Imagine a school canteen. Instead of one person doing everything, there is a cook, a cashier and a server. Each does one job well, and the same cook serves many orders. In programming, a function is like one such worker: a named block of code that does one specific task and can be used again and again.
We have already used functions: main() is a function, and sqrt() , pow() and
getline() are library functions.

items.html: Reusability: Write once, call many times.
Modularity: A large program is divided into small, manageable parts (decomposition, Chapter 4).
Easy debugging: Errors can be found in one function at a time.
Readability: calculateGST(price) is easier to understand than 10 lines of maths.
Teamwork: Different programmers can write different functions.

lessons.title: 7.4 Call by Value and Call by Reference

items.html: Call by value: A copy of the argument is passed. Changes inside the function do not affect the original variable.
Call by reference: The function receives a reference (another name) for the original variable, written with & . Changes inside the function do affect the original.

blocks.code:
After call by value     : x = 10, y = 20
After call by reference : x = 20, y = 10

rows: A copy of the value is passed
A reference to the original is passed
Safe; uses extra memory for the copy
Efficient for large data; can return many results

blocks.html: Real-life example: Call by value is giving a friend a photocopy of your notes — if they scribble on it, your notes are safe. Call by reference is giving them your original notebook.
A parameter can be given a default value. If the caller does not pass that argument, the default is used. Default values must be given from right to left.
float f(float p = 1000, float r, int t); is an error, because defaults must start
from the rightmost parameter.

C++ allows many functions with the same name if their parameter lists differ (in number or type of parameters). The compiler chooses the right one from the arguments. The return type alone cannot make functions different.

blocks.html: The scope of a variable is the part of the program where it can be used.

items.html: Local variable: Declared inside a function or block. Exists only there; destroyed when the block ends.
Global variable: Declared outside all functions. Can be used anywhere in the program.
If a local and a global variable have the same name, the local one is used. Use the scope resolution operator :: to reach the global one.

blocks.code:
Local score  = 5
Global score = 100
Global score in main = 101

blocks.html: Good practice: avoid global variables where possible, because any function can change them, which makes bugs hard to find.

blocks.html: A function that calls itself is called a recursive function. It must have a base case that stops the recursion; otherwise it runs forever.
n! = n × (n − 1)!, and 1! = 1 (base case).
How factorial(4) runs: factorial(4) = 4 × factorial(3) = 4 × 3 × factorial(2) = 4 × 3 × 2 × factorial(1) = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

blocks.html: 1. What is a function? Write two advantages.
Answer: A function is a named block of code that performs a specific task and can be called whenever needed. Advantages: code reusability and easier debugging through modular design.
2. Differentiate between actual and formal arguments.
Answer: Actual arguments are the values passed in the function call (area(5, 3) ); formal parameters are the variables in the function definition that receive them (int area(int l, int b) ).
3. Differentiate between a local and a global variable.
Answer: A local variable is declared inside a function/block and is usable only there; a global variable is declared outside all functions and is usable throughout the program.
4. What is a function prototype? Give an example.
Answer: A declaration of a function that tells the compiler its return type, name and parameter types before it is used. Example: float average(int a, int b, int c);
5. Write the output:
Answer: 10 — the function adds the digits recursively: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1.
6. Write the output: cout << ceil(-2.3) << " " << floor(-2.3) << " " << pow(3, 3);
Answer: -2 -3 27
7. Can two functions differ only by return type? Explain.
Answer: No. In overloading, the parameter lists must differ. int f(int) and float f(int) give a compile error because the call f(5) cannot decide which to use.
8. Write a function to return the cube of a number.
1. Explain call by value and call by reference with a program.
Answer: See 7.4 and Program 7.4. In call by value a copy is passed, so the swap does not affect x and y ; in call by reference (int &a ) the originals are swapped.
2. What is function overloading? Write a program with overloaded functions to find the maximum of two integers, three integers and two doubles.
3. Explain any five functions of <cmath> with examples.
Answer: See the table in 7.8: sqrt(144) = 12, pow(2, 10) = 1024, abs(-25) = 25,
ceil(4.2) = 5, floor(4.8) = 4, round(4.5) = 5.
